newsitem.title: USA: Golden Bear sees charge, short-term lag.
newsitem.headline: Golden Bear sees charge, short-term lag.

text.p: Golden Bear Golf Inc said would take a charge of $570,000, or $0.05 per share, as a result of severance expenses.

In a press release issued Thursday, the company also said there would be some negative short-term effect in the company's results from shifts in operations, renovations and other changes at its Golf Centers and Paragon Construction units.
The severance costs will be recorded in the first quarter. The costs come "in connection with the company's appointment of new presidents in both its Golf Center and Paragon Construction units."

"The new appointments of Scott Colabuono as president of Golden Bear Golf Centers and John Boyd as president of Paragon Construction bring a wealth of financial, operational and marketing experience to these growing business units," said Dick Bellinger, Golden Bear's chief executive.
The press release did not say specifically that the employment of the previous presidents of those units was terminated, and the company was not immediately available to comment.

Golden Bear's stock was down sharply in afternoon trading, falling 2 points, or about 16 percent, to 10-1/2 and touching a new low of 9-1/4. It was one of the top losing stocks on the Nasdaq on a percentage basis.

The company went on to say that it has bought a total of 15 golf centers in the period covering the fiscal 1996 fourth quarter and the first quarter of 1997. The centers will require extensive renovations, which will result in "significant expenditures without commensurate revenues during the conversion process."
Recent changes in the Paragon unit, which the company termed "improvement of systems and personnel," have led to "a lower volume of active business in the first quarter of 1997," Golden Bear said.

The company said the shift at Paragon has "resulted in the successful implementation of improved processes and controls," adding that the unit delayed pursuing project opportunities during the last two fiscal quarters.
The unit now has projects worth more than $35 million in the pipeline, but the work will not begin until the second quarter, the company said.

"While these events have a negative impact on our short-term results, we believe...the steps taken during the first quarter will help us to achieve our long-term goals and improved profitability," Bellinger said in the release.
